methodology: The study utilized the Michael addition reaction of acetoacetates and acrylates to form a polymer scaffold with controlled molecular weight and pendant groups capable of undergoing double addition reactions with acrylates.
research_objective: To develop a robust post-polymerization modification technique that enables the synthesis of innovative functional polymers with tunable properties such as thermal stability, glass transition temperature, and hydrophilicity.

key_findings.finding: Demonstrated the Michael addition reaction of acetoacetates and acrylates as a robust PPM technique with mild conditions (40°C) and high atom economy
Synthesized polymers with tunable thermal stability, glass transition temperature, and hydrophilicity through post-polymerization modification
The PPM reaction using β-ketoesters as a tool for highly functionalized polymers has not been reported previously.

β-ketoesters participate in multi-component reactions such as Hantzsch and Biginelli, playing a key role in the design and synthesis of complex polymers through multi-component polymerization strategies.

The PPM approach has been leveraged to synthesize polymers exhibiting aggregation-induced luminescence (AIE) and produce photo-luminescence polymer materials with customizable mechanical characteristics.

In this work, the Michael addition reaction of acetoacetates and acrylates have been demonstrated Michael addition as a robust PPM technique. The reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer polymerization of commercially Acetoacetate available 2-(acetoacetoxy)ethyl methacrylate provides a polymer scaffold with controlled molecular weight and acetoacetate groups. These pendant groups are capable of undergoing efficient double addition reactions with acrylates, leading to an increased density of functional moieties within the polymeric backbone. This PPM re- action exhibits unique advantages such as mild reaction conditions (at 40 ◦C), rapid kinetics (completion within 1 h), and high atom economy. Consequently, a series of polymers with tunable thermal stability, glass transition temperature, and hydrophilicity have been successfully synthesized. Applications have been demonstrated for both the synthesis of polymers exhibiting aggregation-induced luminescence and the preparation of luminescent materials with adjustable mechanical properties.
